rulings.evidence: Whole dried juniper for the brine. The board has no commodity and no capture match and no near id covers it, so null (pantry-static) rather than a stretch onto another spice; the term is reported absent so the pricing road can rule. 12 berries at 0.2 g each.

Follows this run's 2026-08-28 ruling on the identical phrase; cardamom is a live board id (2 of 7, 10.52), so a REUSE. The 'ground cloves or cardamom' precedent chose cloves only because that line offered either one, which this line does not.
Same-phrase prior ruling from this run, and black-peppercorns is a live board id at 5 of 7 (0.4994 Fareway), so a REUSE. 1 tbsp of whole peppercorns is about 6.5 g, a little lighter than ground.

REFUSED the board's broccoli match: rabe (rapini) is a different vegetable, sold by the bunch at a markedly higher price, and mapping it to broccoli would misprice and misweigh the line. Same-phrase prior ruling this run used broccoli-rabe; one bunch trims to about 340 g.

Dry-cured Italian ham at roughly ten dollars a pound, not deli ham and not bacon; 'very thinly sliced' is how prosciutto is always sold, not a form flip. Matches this run's same-phrase ruling; board has no commodity and no capture match, so the term is reported absent.

Reduced, sweetened balsamic sold as glaze: 40 cal and 10 g carbs per tbsp against vinegar's 15 cal and 3 g, a different product in a different bottle at a different price, so the balsamic-vinegar form flip is refused. Matches this run's same-phrase ruling; board absent, term reported.

Tap water for the brine: no shopper buys it and no commodity claims it, so no id and no cost. It is kept in the lines array with its weight so the brine still reads correctly, and its DB row is all zeroes.

REFUSED both the board's oranges match and the Orange Juice near-row: a small alcohol-based flavouring bottle is neither fresh fruit nor juice, in price class or in gram weight. Null is pantry-static and safe; the term is reported absent.

new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Dry-cured, unsmoked Italian ham sold in 3 to 4 oz packs at roughly 10 to 16 dollars a pound. It is not deli-ham (cooked, wet-cured lunch meat at about 5 dollars a pound), not spiral-ham or diced-ham (cooked whole-muscle roast and convenience dice), and not bacon or pancetta (smoked or belly cuts). The estate's own lookup for this term found no commodity in any namespace and no capture match, and no vocabulary row shares a core word with it. A prior ruling in this same run already settled the identical phrase to this id, so if it has since been minted this is a REUSE and not a proposal.

A separate shelf product from balsamic vinegar: the vinegar is reduced with sweetener to a pourable syrup, printing 40 cal and 10 g carbs per tbsp against vinegar's 15 cal and 3 g, in a squeeze bottle at a higher price per ounce. Bridging it to balsamic-vinegar would be wrong on price and on gram weight, which is why the pre-resolve flagged the syrup/vinegar form difference rather than aliasing it. Board reports no commodity and no capture match. A prior ruling this run used this same id for the identical phrase.

Rapini is a distinct brassica sold as a leafy bunch, not a crown of broccoli, and it is routinely two to three times broccoli's price per pound; the board's broccoli match is a different food. A prior ruling this run already settled the identical phrase to broccoli-rabe, so if that id exists this is a REUSE and no new mint is needed, exactly like the brown-lentils case where only the vocabulary row was missing.
